LESSON: TOPOGRAPHICAL MAPS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.1: Topographical maps

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Topographical maps. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are topographical maps important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe human activities on topographical maps
2. use creative thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: TOPOGRAPHICAL MAPS
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Topographical maps helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: TOPOGRAPHICAL MAPS
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Describe human activities on topographical maps

What this means
In this part you learn to describe human activities on topographical maps. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe human activities on topographical maps.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Topographical maps” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe human activities on topographical maps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use creative thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps

What this means
In this part you learn to use creative thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use creative thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Topographical maps.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use creative thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Topographical maps is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Topographical maps” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: describe human activities on topographical maps)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Topographical maps. (skill: use creative thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Topographical maps to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe human activities on topographical maps.
3. Practise this skill: use creative thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Topographical maps from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Topographical maps: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Topographical maps?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are topographical maps important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Topographical maps means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe human activities on topographical maps.
5. Be able to: use creative thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
